## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double anonymous: the live instructions say that once the editor has assessed suitability the paper is "double anonymous peer reviewed by two independent, anonymous expert" referees, and warn that anonymity cannot be guaranteed for a manuscript shared on a preprint server (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=tsep20&page=instructions, read 2026-11-24). The live about page adds: "All research articles published in this journal have undergone peer review, based on initial editor screening and anonymized refereeing by at least two referees" (https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/tsep20/about-this-journal). The 2022-08-10 instructions copy said double blind; the 2022-06-15 aims copy said the same as the live about page. Retrieved 2026-11-24 |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No journal-specific source read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No source read stating that reports are published |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev reports an average of 1.5 review rounds and 2.0 review reports per manuscript from 2 reviews (https://scirev.org/journal/social-epistemology/). The 7 APA-survey reports show 3 revise-and-resubmit, 4 rejection and 0 direct acceptance as first verdict, and 3 acceptances after revision (https://apasurvey.philx.org/surveys/export_csv) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No source read |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Partly. The live instructions page (read in a real browser 2026-11-24) asks every submission to include a "Declaration of generative AI use": a statement disclosing whether and how generative AI was used in the research and manuscript preparation (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=tsep20&page=instructions). The 2022-08-10 copy predates this. The publisher-wide Taylor & Francis policy applies |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Use is allowed with a mandatory disclosure statement |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory disclosure; same rubric as the Mind entry) |
| **Summary** | Publisher policy, retrieved 2026-11-23: AI tools cannot be credited as authors; any AI use must be acknowledged, naming the tool and version, how it was used and why; AI may not be used to create or alter research images or results; unrevised AI output may trigger an editorial investigation. Editors and reviewers must not upload unpublished manuscripts into AI tools, and reviewers must not use AI to write review reports |
| **Source URL** | https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/ |

### Preprint Policy

> Publisher-level policy, not journal-specific. Source: https://authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com/research-impact/sharing-versions-of-journal-articles/ (retrieved 2026-11-23). The journal-specific embargo was not looked up.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | The author's original manuscript may be shared widely, including on non-commercial preprint servers such as arXiv or SocArXiv; posting it before submission does not count as duplicate publication. The journal's own instructions copy (2022-08-10) adds that anonymity cannot be guaranteed for a paper already on a preprint server |
| Under review | Blank | The page speaks of the original manuscript and does not separately address the under-review stage |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes, with embargo | Personal website or social media any time after publication; repositories and scholarly networks after an embargo. Embargo: the page says embargoes are typically 12 months for the Science, Technology and Medicine portfolio and 18 months for the Social Sciences and Humanities portfolio, counted from first online publication of the Version of Record, and that each journal's own embargo is listed separately in the publisher's open access cost finder (publisher page above; this journal's own embargo was not looked up, so 18 months is the typical figure for its portfolio, not a confirmed value) |
| Version of Record | Eprint links and open-access sharing | Free eprint links (up to 50 uses) or eReader links; open access articles have no sharing restrictions, per the same page |

## Format

> Source for every row unless stated: the journal's live instructions for authors (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=tsep20&page=instructions), read in a real browser on 2026-11-24; the page prints no date. Retrieved 2026-11-24. The Wayback copy of 2022-08-10 is older; rows that rest only on it say so.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | The instructions list "original articles" and English-language manuscripts only. The aims copy (2022-06-15) describes "exchanges" that are collective products (critical syntheses, open peer commentaries, interviews, applications, provocations, reviews, responses). OpenAlex types 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23: 329 articles, 5 editorials, 2 errata, 1 review (https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=primary_location.source.id:S113020877) |
| **Word limit** | "A typical paper for this journal should be between 6000 and 8000 words", inclusive of tables, references, figure or table captions and endnotes; authors are asked to include a word count (live instructions, read 2026-11-24). Crossref page ranges give a median article length of 14 pages (25th to 75th percentile 12 to 17 pages) across 336 of 337 records, 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0269-1728) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The live instructions phrase 6000-8000 words as typical ("a typical paper"); no statement on exceptions |
| **Abstract limit** | Unstructured abstract of 200 words (live instructions, read 2026-11-24). The 3 to 4 keywords of the 2022-08-10 copy were not found in the passages of the live page read; the live structure line only lists keywords after the abstract |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the 6000-8000 words |
| **Supplementary material** | Supplemental material (video, dataset, files) is published via Figshare |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit stated. Figures at 1200 dpi line art, 600 dpi greyscale, 300 dpi colour; editable tables. Colour in print is charged (GBP 300 per figure for the first four, GBP 50 from the fifth) |
| **Style / submission format** | Any spelling style if consistent; single quotation marks; Word format; ScholarOne submission system; Crossref similarity screening; Word template available. The text read gives no instruction to anonymise the manuscript body, although review is double blind |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One scope statement is published by the journal: the aims copy (2022-06-15) describes a forum for philosophical and social scientific enquiry into the production, assessment and validation of knowledge, covering both empirical research on origination and transmission of knowledge and normative considerations (https://web.archive.org/web/20220615115913/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/journalInformation?show=aimsScope&journalCode=tsep20).
- **What kind of engagement?** Engagement with how knowledge is produced, transmitted or validated socially. In the 330 abstracts, "I argue, we argue or this paper/article/essay argues" appears in 116 (35.2%), a sign of argument-led essays.
- **Article type and length**: original articles of about 6000 to 8000 words including references, with an unstructured 200-word abstract and 3 to 4 keywords (instructions copy 2022-08-10, https://web.archive.org/web/20220810175355/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=tsep20). Collective "exchanges" are also published per the aims copy.
- **Open call seen**: none on 2026-11-23 (calls-for-papers site search and web search found no open call).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No source states what happens to out-of-scope submissions.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are OpenAlex works of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (337 records, 330 with abstract) whose title or abstract matches the regex in AI-Research Notes; shares use 330 as denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 1 | "experiment-, experimental or randomised" 3 of 330 (0.9%); "quantitative, statistical or regression" 8 (2.4%) |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | "interview" 10 of 330 (3.0%); "qualitative" 8 (2.4%); "ethnograph- or fieldwork" 9 (2.7%) |
| Autoethnography | 0 | "autoethnograph-" 0 of 330 abstracts and 0 of 337 titles |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | "philosoph-" 64 of 330 (19.4%); "theoretical or theory" 69 (20.9%); "conceptual" 21 (6.4%) |
| Mixed methods | 0 | "mixed methods" 0 of 330 |
| Meta-analysis | 1 | "systematic review, meta-analysis or scoping review" 1 of 330 (0.3%); the 2023 item "Promoting Interdisciplinary Research Collaboration: A Systematic Review, a Critical Literature Review, and a Pathway Forward" has 146 OpenAlex citations (https://doi.org/10.1080/02691728.2023.2172694) |
| Formal modelling (added row) | 2 | "Bayesian, formal model, agent-based, simulation, game theory or modelling" 6 of 330 abstracts (1.8%) |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Live board block lists 50 people (see Editorial-board geography). Disciplines are not listed on the page, so no discipline split is given. Topic mix of published work: 110 of 337 works have OpenAlex primary topic "Epistemology, Ethics, and Metaphysics" and 68 "Feminist Epistemology and Gender Studies" | https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/tsep20/about-this-journal (live board block, counted 2026-11-24); OpenAlex works API, retrieved 2026-11-23; board composition may change |
| **Reviewer list size** | The page names no separate reviewer list; only the 50 editor, officer and advisory-board entries (1 + 5 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 37 = 50) | Live board block, counted 2026-11-24 |
| **Review model** | Double anonymous, two independent anonymous expert referees after editor screening; the about page says anonymized refereeing by at least two referees | Live instructions and about page (URLs in Peer Review), read 2026-11-24 |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Small author samples only. ### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | The instructions copy (2022-08-10) points to the publisher's general publishing-ethics guidance (https://web.archive.org/web/20220810175355/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=tsep20) and contains no journal-specific ethics-approval rule in the text read. Work is mostly non-empirical by keyword count (interview 10 of 330 abstracts), which is not itself an ethics rule |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers dominate: 244 of 329 articles (74.2%) dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (OpenAlex authorships) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | The instructions copy asks for full affiliation "where the research was conducted" and states no independent-scholar rule (URL above). 2 of the 39 board members on the archived board page are listed as independent scholars (https://web.archive.org/web/20230523101129/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/journalInformation?show=editorialBoard&journalCode=tsep20) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | The journal applies the publisher's Basic Data Sharing Policy: sharing is encouraged, not required, where human-subject protection permits; a data availability statement is encouraged (instructions copy 2022-08-10) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Review is double blind per the instructions copy, yet the same copy asks for names and affiliations on the cover page and warns that a preprint removes any anonymity guarantee; pre-submission preprints are allowed (https://authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com/research-impact/sharing-versions-of-journal-articles/). Crossref similarity screening applies to all submissions |
| **AI use** | Disclosure statement required; AI cannot be an author (https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/), retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; 142 of 329 recent articles are hybrid open access in OpenAlex; no submission or page charges (instructions copy 2022-08-10); the APC amount was not obtained |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 3. Per layer: OpenAlex counts (methods, topics, countries, types) 4 (330 of 337 records have abstracts, regexes are word-bounded and listed below); publisher-wide policies 4; journal-specific policies and guidelines 4 (live instructions and about pages read in a real browser 2026-11-24; undated; the board block says Updated 22-09-2026; the 2022-2023 Wayback copies are kept as labelled older figures); experiential layer 2 (APA Journal Survey n=7 reports, SciRev n=2 reviews, self-reported and anonymous, possibly overlapping).

**Method note:** OpenAlex works were fetched with page-based paging (no key, no email, one request per 2 seconds; no HTTP 429 occurred). Counts are computed locally over title plus reconstructed abstract with the regexes below (case-insensitive unless a name is marked case-sensitive); word-boundary matching avoids substring inflation. Crossref lists the same 337 records but none carries an abstract, so Crossref was used only for the record count and page ranges. Counts are lower bounds for any topic expressed without the listed words. The research pass's own scoring convention is stated in Methodological Preferences.

**Regexes used** (all with word boundaries): interview `interviews?|interviewed`; survey `surveys?|questionnaires?`; qualitative `qualitative`; quantitative `quantitative|statistical|regression`; experiment `experiments?|experimental|randomi[sz]ed`; case study `case stud(y|ies)`; ethnography `ethnograph\w*|fieldwork`; formal `Bayesian|formal model\w*|agent-based|simulation\w*|game[- ]theor\w*|model(l)?ing`; review `systematic review|meta-analys\w+|scoping review`; conceptual `conceptual`; philosophical `philosoph\w+`; theoretical `theoretical|theory`; mixed `mixed[- ]methods?`; autoethnography `autoethnograph\w*`; empirical `empirical\w*`; epistemic injustice `epistemic (in)?justice|testimonial injustice|hermeneutical injustice`; gender `gender\w*|feminis\w+|women`; race `rac(e|ial|ism|ist)|whiteness`; decolonial `decoloni\w+|indigenous|postcolonial\w*|colonial\w*`; queer `queer|trans(gender)?|LGBT\w*|sexual orientation`; religion `religio\w+|Christian\w*|Islam\w*|Buddhis\w+|theolog\w+`; conspiracy `conspirac\w+`; misinformation `misinformation|disinformation|fake news|post-truth`; COVID `COVID\w*|pandemic|vaccin\w+`; climate `climate`; AI `artificial intelligence|AI|ChatGPT|machine learning|large language model\w*|LLMs?`; politics `political|politics|populis\w+|democra\w+`; expert `expert\w*`; argue `I argue|we argue|this (paper|article|essay) argues?`; first person `I|we|my|our` (case-sensitive).

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Language**: the 2022-08-10 instructions copy states that only English-language manuscripts are published (Format); this sentence was not located in the live page text read on 2026-11-24.
- **Length**: a typical paper is 6000 to 8000 words including references, endnotes and captions (Format, live instructions read 2026-11-24). Whether exceptions are granted is not stated.
- **AI use**: undisclosed generative-AI use or AI-altered research images breach the publisher policy (AI Policy, https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/).
- **Anonymity**: review is double anonymous and a preprint removes any anonymity guarantee (Peer Review; Practical Concerns), so a paper already on a public server may not stay anonymous in review.
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read; ethics-approval rules are not stated in the passages of the live instructions read (Practical Concerns).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the publisher's live block gives an average of 51 days to first decision and 114 days to the first post-review decision (no period printed; older copy of 2022-06-18: median 52 days), whereas 7 author reports to the APA survey average 4.5 months to a response (median 3.5, range 2.0 to 9.5) and SciRev's 2 reviews give 4.8 months for the first round (Review Cycle Time). The gap between the publisher figure and the author samples is large; the samples are small.
- **Open access cost**: green deposit of the accepted manuscript is subject to an embargo that the publisher page gives as typically 12 months (STM) and 18 months (social sciences and humanities), with each journal's own embargo on a separate list that was not looked up, so this journal's embargo is unverified (Preprint Policy); gold open access carries an APC whose amount was not obtained (Open Access).
- **Anonymisation work**: names and affiliations go on the cover page while review is double blind (Peer Review; Format), so the author must keep identifying content out of the manuscript body; the text read gives no further instruction.

### Best Suited For

- Argument-led conceptual and philosophical papers on knowledge, testimony, expertise and epistemic injustice: "philosoph-" appears in 64 of 330 abstracts and "epistemic injustice" terms in 55 (Orientation, Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Work on misinformation, conspiracy theories, public expertise and AI-related knowledge: 22, 32, 56 and 23 of 330 abstracts respectively (Sensitive Topics).
- Single-author essays: 244 of 329 articles are single-author (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Primarily empirical or experimental studies: "experiment-" appears in 3 of 330 abstracts, "survey" in 5 and "interview" in 10 (Methodological Preferences). These counts show such work is rare here, not that it is rejected.
- Authors who need a dependable turnaround figure: the publisher figure (52 days) and the author samples (months) disagree widely (Review Cycle Time).
- Work needing a stated open call or special-issue home: no open call was found on 2026-11-23 (Publication Frequency).
